backtest_protocol.execution_model: Earnings snapshot fields are read from canonical daily snapshots dated at or before the signal date. OHLCV confirmation is observed through the signal-date close; paper entry is the next available open with production entry slippage; exit is ten trading days after the signal with target-side sell slippage and ROUND_TRIP_COST_PCT.

gate2.note: The sleeve uses only same-day and trailing OHLCV fields plus next-open/exit prices available to the replay. It does not ask LLM or production to infer hidden fields.
runtime_fields: SPY OHLCV rows for same-window relative strength

gate3.note: No core filter or live entry rule was added. The target source is additive default-off paper, so core survival is unchanged.

gate_questions.1_alpha_hypothesis: candidate_pool / entry: imminent earnings can create expectation drift when durable historical surprise quality is confirmed by current RS, trend, high close, and liquidity.

2_history_check.estimate_revision_ledger_preflight: Canonical windows had no rows where pit_safe_flag and estimate_revision_usable were both true, so a revision-ledger candidate pool is data-blocked for this run.
2_history_check.exp-20260508-001: A 22-45 day pre-earnings risk replay was not a retained candidate source. This run tests an additive stock pool using earnings snapshot quality plus OHLCV confirmation.
2_history_check.exp-20260508-013: 8-21 day pre-earnings variants were unstable. This run does not retune them; it tests the imminent 1-7 day phase.
2_history_check.exp-20260531-001: The 22-45 day pre-earnings surprise/revision RS pool regressed aggregate EV. This run changes the timing bucket to 1-7 days and removes the unusable revision gate.

gate_questions.4_acceptance_standard: Same three docs/backtesting.md windows; positive aggregate EV/PnL; 3/3 EV-improved windows; no PnL-regressed window; >=20 paper trades across all 3 windows; drawdown drift <=0.5pp; survival >=5%; concentration inside guardrails. A positive replay lead is not retained without a shared default-off adapter.

hypothesis: Earnings-imminent stocks with durable positive historical EPS surprise behavior and liquid RS/trend confirmation may add a production-visible free-data candidate-pool sleeve.
interpretation: The earnings-imminent surprise/RS source did not clear Gate 4. Do not promote it or retry adjacent imminent-earnings snapshot thresholds on the frozen windows without new forward rows or a different expectation-quality field.
next_evidence_needed: If revisited, use closed forward replacement-value rows or a materially richer free-data field such as reliable current-quarter guidance, surprise dispersion, or a now-usable PIT revision ledger.

source_definition: canonical daily earnings snapshot row exists at or before signal date
at least 3 historical surprises are positive
EPS estimate is present in the PIT snapshot
ticker closes above prior 50-day moving average
top-1 selected paper entry per signal date

prediction.confidence_reason: The 1-7 day bucket is distinct from the rejected 22-45 day surprise/revision sleeve and avoids unusable estimate_revision_ledger rows, but nearby pre-earnings timing experiments were unstable.

production_impact.promotion_requirement: A retained result would still require a shared default-off paper adapter and parity tests before any daily report or live/default behavior changes.

production_parity.parity_note: No production code path is changed. Even if Gate 4 is positive, the lead is not promoted or retained as a strategy rule until a shared default-off adapter and parity tests read the same quant/data_paths.py daily earnings snapshots in replay and production surfaces.

why_not_other_changes: Skipped LLM soft-ranking because candidate-level attribution remains sparse. Skipped estimate_revision_ledger because a preflight found no PIT-usable rows in the canonical windows. Skipped Companyfacts/VBB/VCP/FINRA/state-surface scalar retunes because the playbook asks for forward rows or materially new fields. This tests one different free-data candidate-pool source only.
